narrative_before: This is a documented CTID emulation of OceanLotus (APT32, Vietnam-nexus), modelling the group's real macOS/Linux intrusion TTPs. The user Hope Potter double-clicks a macOS application disguised as a Word document (conkylan.app) delivered by spearphishing, detonating a payload that establishes a Launch Agent and connects to C2. OceanLotus performs local discovery on the macOS host, reads the .ssh folder, and exfiltrates known_hosts and bash history; the history reveals that Hope sends files to a Linux file server via SCP. OceanLotus downloads Rota Jakiro to the macOS host, uses SCP/SSH to transfer it to the Linux server and make it executable, and executes it there - collecting host information, finding and staging .pdf files, compressing them into rota.tar.gz, and exfiltrating to the C2 server.

ambiguities: Documented emulation of real OceanLotus/APT32 TTPs; year 2020 chosen as a representative basis (Rota Jakiro era).
Only two hosts are named in the plan (Hope Potter's macOS laptop and the Linux file server); no additional hosts invented.
The macOS host is treated as the entry and the Linux server as the single lateral hop (meets entry + >=1 hop).
